# Soak turn content is a Claude-authored example bank, lightly varied at runtime — not freely generated by the local driver

**Status:** accepted

CTS.md's own framing splits the work: "Claude designs the plan, a local model grinds through execution." Its loop pseudocode didn't actually settle who writes each turn's payload text, and the literal reading of "a local LLM drives a blueprint" could mean the local model freely authors synthetic content per turn.

For a target like Shenny that's a real risk, not just a style preference: its content is real domestic-conflict subject matter (`dataPolicy: restricted`), and an unattended 8B local model free-generating thousands of synthetic "escalated" or "ambiguous-third-party-behavior" narratives for hours has no review step until the run is already over. It's also less repeatable — comparing two soak runs' findings is harder when the underlying content differs unpredictably between them.

**Decided:** the blueprint's `variationPool` carries a Claude-authored bank of example narratives (in the `.ts` blueprint file itself) per variation bucket. At runtime, the local driver only selects an example and lightly varies it (word substitution, length trim/pad, detail reordering) — it does not author new scenarios from scratch. This matches CTS.md's own division of labor literally: Claude designs the scenario space (including its content) once, at design time; the local model's runtime job is variation and pacing, not open-ended authorship.

**Consequence:** turn-selection itself (which variation fires next, respecting per-pipeline budgets) needs no LLM call at all — it's plain scheduling code. Only the "lightly vary this example's text" step calls the local model, which narrows what an unattended run actually depends on the driver model to get right.
